name: Shishak
title: Egypt's pharaoh who invaded Judah
summary: Shishak (also known as Shoshenq I) was an Egyptian pharaoh from the 22nd dynasty who invaded the kingdom of Judah during the reign of King Rehoboam. He plundered the temple and the king's palace in Jerusalem, taking with him the treasures that Solomon had gathered. His campaign is one of the most important links between biblical history and Egyptian archaeology.

keyEvents.title: Jeroboam flees to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Jeroboam, who later became the first king of northern Israel, fled to Shishak in Egypt to escape King Solomon's anger. Shishak gave him protection until Solomon died.

keyEvents.title: The Invasion of Judah
keyEvents.description: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, Shishak marched up against Jerusalem with a huge army because the people had been unfaithful to the Lord.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Shemaiah's Warning
keyEvents.description: The prophet Shemaiah explained to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah that Shishak's invasion was God's judgment because they had abandoned the Lord. The leaders humbled themselves before God.

keyEvents.title: The Plundering of the Temple and Palace
keyEvents.description: Shishak took the treasures from the Lord's temple and from the king's palace, including the gold shields that Solomon had made. Rehoboam replaced them with bronze shields.

keyEvents.title: God's Partial Grace toward Judah
keyEvents.description: Because Rehoboam and the leaders humbled themselves, the Lord did not completely destroy them, but they became Shishak's servants so that they might learn the difference between serving the Lord and serving foreign kings.

keyEvents.title: Shishak's Campaign Documented in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: 2 Chronicles gives detailed information about Shishak's army, which included 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen, and countless soldiers from Libya, Sukki, and Cush.
